players.product: wafer-level burn-in systems (FOX) with WaferPak full-wafer contactors, and Sonoma package-level burn-in, for AI accelerators and silicon photonics

quarterly_data.signal: Aehr's earnings release: net revenue for the fiscal 2026 fourth quarter (ended May 29, 2026) was $18.8 million, compared to $14.1 million in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025, and quarterly bookings were a record $60.7 million. Effective backlog, including bookings since May 29, 2026, is $100.6 million. Fiscal 2026 net revenue was $50.0 million, compared to $59.0 million in fiscal 2025.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 FY2026 revenue $18.8 million (vs $14.1 million); bookings $60.7 million; effective backlog $100.6 million; fiscal 2026 revenue $50.0 million (vs $59.0 million)

quarterly_data.signal: Aehr's release says its package-level burn-in business for AI processors received record follow-on production orders from its lead hyperscale customer (not named; described as a premier large-scale data center provider) for Sonoma systems supporting high-volume AI processor production burn-in, and that this customer is forecasting a substantial expansion of Sonoma system purchases for a second device with twice the power per package of the first device it uses Sonoma systems for today.

players.product: burn-in and reliability screening for optical devices — data-center transceivers, chip-to-chip I/O and silicon photonics (FOX wafer-level and Sonoma package-level)

quarterly_data.signal: Aehr's release says its lead silicon photonics customer is ramping, with follow-on orders over the past year and more already in the current fiscal year for fully automated wafer-level burn-in systems for AI optical I/O and data center interconnects. Its newest major silicon photonics customer (not named; described as a global leader in networking products and solutions) has provided Aehr a forecast for additional systems this calendar year as it ramps capacity to support next-generation hyperscale data center deployments.
